title: Where can you find free practice cases from the consulting firms themselves?
description: A list of the free, official practice cases and interview guides published by McKinsey, BCG, Bain, Deloitte and other firms, and how to use them.
hook: The best practice material is often free, and it comes straight from the firms you are applying to. Official cases show you exactly how each firm thinks about its interviews. Here is where to find them, and how to get the most out of them.
body:
McKinsey

McKinsey's interviewing page explains its problem-solving and personal experience interviews and includes several practice cases, such as Beautify, with suggested approaches. These are interviewer-led, like the real thing.

BCG

BCG's careers site has a case interview preparation page with tips, interactive cases and a downloadable written case. Its interview-process page explains the skill, case and team interviews.

Bain

Bain's interview preparation pages cover case interviews, experience interviews and other formats, with practice cases such as a coffee shop case and a fashion case.

Deloitte

Deloitte runs a free, interactive case interview practice tool with cases for different practices, plus a case interview tips page.

Other firms

Kearney, Oliver Wyman, Roland Berger, Accenture, OC&C, Simon-Kucher and Strategy& also publish practice material on their websites. Search the firm's name with "case interview" on its careers site.

How to use official cases

  1. Start with one case from the firm you care most about, to see its style.
  2. Do it out loud, timed, before reading the suggested answer.
  3. Compare your structure with theirs, and note one thing to improve.
  4. Then practise with a partner using cases in the same style.

On PrepForCase

Our free casebook has over 100 cases with worked answers and interviewer scripts, and our drills train the individual skills.

Turn an official sample into three practice sessions

You can get more value from a single official sample case than from skimming ten case descriptions. First pass: attempt the case without reading the suggested solution. Write your opening recap, issue tree, quantitative workings and final answer. Second pass: compare the supplied reasoning with yours, but label differences as missing logic, weaker prioritisation or different valid approaches rather than simply right and wrong.

Third pass: turn the case into a 25-minute mock interview. Have a partner hold back information until you ask for it, pause after each exhibit, and push you to explain the business implication of every number. This trains the conversation, not just the written answer.

For example, if a sample case suggests a market could sustain five stores, don't stop at the store count. Ask how the number changes if average revenue is 15% lower or the client captures half the expected market share. Then explain whether the investment recommendation would change. These variations are your own practice, not reproductions of the firm's proprietary questions or solutions. Always consult the current official recruiting site for the authentic source material.
